Where it began

Umar Akmal was born in Lahore on 26 May 1990 and went to school with the Beaconhouse School System. He grew up in a house full of cricket. He is the youngest brother of Kamran and Adnan Akmal, both of whom kept wicket for Pakistan, and Babar Azam is his cousin. Few families can have argued about the batting order over dinner with quite so much expertise.

He played for Pakistan at the 2008 Under-19 World Cup in Malaysia and went straight into first-class cricket with Sui Northern Gas. In only his sixth first-class game he hit 248 from 225 balls, and two matches later he made an unbeaten 186. A tour with Pakistan A to Australia in 2009 brought scores of 100 not out and 130 in the unofficial Tests, and a hundred from 68 balls in the first one-day game. The selectors did not need much more convincing.

The player

His Test debut came at Dunedin in November 2009, and it was one to keep. On the third day he made 129 from 160 balls, sharing a stand of more than a hundred with Kamran, and he added a fifty in the second innings. Only one Pakistani before him, Fawad Alam, had made a hundred on Test debut away from home. He ended that New Zealand tour with 379 runs at 63.16, the most by anyone in the series.

In all he played 16 Tests between 2009 and 2011, scoring 1,003 runs at 35.82 with one hundred and six fifties, and he held 12 catches. After his last Test, against Zimbabwe in 2011, his cricket carried on in the one-day and Twenty20 game for several more years.

What made him special

He batted the way most people only dream of batting: on the attack. In his second Test he came in at number five and made 52 from 33 balls, and he had already hit a match-winning hundred in only his third one-day international, against Sri Lanka. His first World Cup innings was a 71 from 52 balls that earned him the match award.

He was not a wicketkeeper by trade, but when the team needed someone to take the gloves he took them, as his brothers had before him. The keeping was always more willing than polished, which is perhaps why the family job stayed mostly with Kamran and Adnan.

Away from the middle

He was a much-travelled Twenty20 batsman. In the first season of the Pakistan Super League, in 2016, he was Lahore Qalandars' top scorer and the leading run-maker in the whole tournament, with 335 runs and four fifties. He also played in the Caribbean, in Bangladesh, in Sri Lanka and for Leicestershire in England. At home he won the first-class title with Habib Bank Limited in 2018-19, and again with Central Punjab, when he was man of the match in the final.

And finally

As a boy his stated dream was simply to play for Pakistan alongside his elder brother Kamran. In his very first Test he did more than that: the two of them batted together and turned the match around. Most dreams do not come true quite so neatly.
